items.headline: White House urges easing cyber liability to spur AI disclosure
items.summary: Officials from Trump's AI task force recommended agencies ease cyber liability policies to incentivize AI companies to report critical incidents. The move could reshape how AI-related security breaches are disclosed and regulated.

items.headline: Bloomberg researchers present six AI finance papers at ICAIF 2026
items.summary: Bloomberg's AI Engineering group is presenting research on trade execution, liquidity, and financial tokenization at the ACM conference in Milan. The work highlights AI's growing role in solving hard quantitative finance problems.

items.headline: AI predicts actionable genomic alterations from stained slides
items.summary: A new study in npj Precision Oncology shows AI can predict actionable genomic alterations directly from H&E-stained tissue slides. The approach could accelerate cancer diagnostics without expensive genomic sequencing.

items.headline: Google brings Gemini 4 Hydrogen to Search globally
items.summary: Google upgraded Search worldwide with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, enabling more intuitive, visual, and precise answers through simultaneous queries and structured results. The update intensifies the AI-powered search race against OpenAI and others.

items.headline: Economist warns investors should expect an AI crash
items.summary: The Economist argues that soaring AI valuations and massive capital spending may not be sustainable, raising crash risks. The analysis questions whether the AI boom can generate enough revenue to justify investment.

items.headline: Fed's Barr warns AI could drive serious job disruption
items.summary: Fed official Michael Barr said AI could begin displacing workers at scale, with the labor share hitting a record low of 52.8% in Q2 2026. He urged policymakers to prepare for widening inequality.

items.headline: Jensen Huang's exit raises questions about Nvidia's future
items.summary: CNBC examines the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia following Jensen Huang's departure amid a security investigation. His exit raises concerns about the company's strategy as rivals like Google ramp up AI chip competition.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster Flash successor
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more capable but pricier successor to its Flash model line. It escalates the model competition against OpenAI's Luna, Meta's Ember, and Anthropic's Haiku.

items.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share
items.summary: Anthropic set its IPO price range, with institutional demand reportedly stronger than SpaceX's at the same stage. The listing could raise around $64.4 billion and value the company as one of the biggest AI debuts ever.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO could raise as much as $64.4 billion
items.summary: Anthropic's latest draft prospectus shows the IPO could raise up to $64.4 billion, seeking a valuation about 20% below market expectations to encourage bidding. Investors are watching it for clues about rival OpenAI's planned debut.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon now publicly available, undercuts rivals on price
items.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to all developers, pricing it at a quarter of Claude Fable 5.2's rates while leading on some agentic benchmarks. The aggressive pricing escalates the frontier model price war.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model opens to developers and scientists
items.summary: Google made its Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, touting state-of-the-art cybersecurity and agentic coding. It marks a major expansion of the Gemini 4 family.

items.headline: November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence to Pixel 10
items.summary: Google's November Pixel Drop introduced Gemini Intelligence to Pixel 10 devices alongside custom widgets and the new Pixel Tag. The update deepens on-device AI integration across Google's hardware lineup.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled Fable 5.2 for coding and agents and restricted-access Mythos 5.2 for cybersecurity and life sciences, with Fable leading on 13 of 15 benchmarks and 20% lower API costs. It is the company's first frontier release since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow AI development.

items.headline: Anthropic buys $3.4 billion in natural gas turbines for power
items.summary: Facing AI's acute power crunch, Anthropic is spending $3.4 billion on Caterpillar gas turbines capable of generating up to 1.7 gigawatts. The move marks a rare shift for a company that historically rents rather than owns infrastructure.

items.headline: CodeRabbit ships 20x more software using OpenAI Codex
items.summary: CodeRabbit uses OpenAI models and Codex to govern AI-generated code and ship 20 times more software with the same engineering team. The case study highlights the growing impact of agentic coding on developer productivity.

items.headline: OpenAI brings businesses into ChatGPT with new commerce features
items.summary: OpenAI launched tools letting businesses claim their presence and connect with customers directly inside ChatGPT. The move expands ChatGPT into a decision-making and commerce platform.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils two new models ahead of landmark IPO
items.summary: Anthropic's first frontier models since September's call to pace AI development went through rigorous safety testing and new post-launch monitoring tools. The releases position Claude competitively just weeks before the company's expected Wall Street debut.

items.headline: OpenAI releases Images 2.6 with faster, more controllable generation
items.summary: OpenAI launched Images 2.6, offering faster iteration, more editing control, GIF animation, and new API capabilities. The update strengthens OpenAI's position in AI image generation.

items.headline: Menlo Ventures: enterprise AI spending hits $177 billion in 2026
items.summary: Menlo Ventures' State of Enterprise AI report found spending jumped 5.4x from $33 billion to $177 billion in one year as AI agents take over workflows. The data signals rapidly accelerating enterprise demand despite Wall Street skepticism.
